checks.title: Production dependencies are pinned to exact versions
checks.why: An unpinned requirement resolves at install time, so production can receive a release that was published after the code was tested. This is also the window a compromised package upload exploits.
checks.action: Pin every production requirement to an exact version, generated from a resolver lock rather than edited by hand, and install with hashes where your toolchain supports it.

verify.expect: Every production requirement carries an exact version, or the project uses a lock file that does.

checks.title: No virtual environment directory is tracked in git
checks.why: A committed environment carries compiled platform-specific binaries and often a pip config or token file. It also makes every dependency change an unreviewable diff of thousands of files.
checks.action: Remove the environment directory from the index, add it to .gitignore, and rebuild it from the pinned requirements in the deploy.

verify.cmd: git ls-files venv .venv env virtualenv | head -5
verify.expect: Nothing is listed. Any path echoed back is a tracked environment directory.

checks.title: No compiled bytecode is tracked in git
checks.why: Stale .pyc files tracked in git can shadow the source they were built from on an interpreter that trusts them, producing a deploy that runs code no longer present in the repository.
checks.action: Remove any tracked bytecode from the index and add the cache directories to .gitignore.

checks.title: The installed dependency set has no unresolved conflicts
checks.why: Pip will complete an install that leaves incompatible versions in place, and the resulting failure surfaces later as an import error or a subtle behaviour change rather than as a failed deploy.
checks.action: Run a dependency consistency check as part of the build and fail the build on conflicts rather than discovering them in production.
